title: Lena and the Verdict
premise: Retired detective Juniper Yarrow, now barely keeping his bookshop afloat, is hired by a nervous stranger who pays triple to prove that a murder scheduled for the winter solstice will never happen — and to find Lena Marsh, the only witness who can stop it. Everyone in the river town of Calder's Bend insists Lena died years ago, but Juniper's old case files say otherwise: her death was recorded, sealed, and signed off by people who are now judges and councilmen. As the solstice approaches, Juniper uncovers a conspiracy built on a falsified verdict from twenty years past, one that gave the town's most powerful family its fortune. In the end, Juniper finds Lena alive in hiding, exposes the corrupted verdict at a public hearing on the eve of the murder, and chooses to reopen his detective practice — with Lena as his partner.
about_author: Ulyana Ravensworth is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent fifteen years transcribing verdicts before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about small towns where the paperwork lies, and lives near a river she refuses to name.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Juniper Yarrow's POV. A gaunt stranger named Corliss walks into the failing bookshop and pays triple rate to prove a murder hasn't happened yet — naming no victim, only a date. Juniper, proud of never taking an unclosable case, accepts against his better judgment. The beat is wary curiosity masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Date That Hasn't Come
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He digs into the solstice date and finds it matches the anniversary of a sealed 2003 inquest: the death of witness Lena Marsh. The emotional beat is unease — the file is too clean, too quickly produced, as if someone wanted it found.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, with a brief interlude from barmaid Tessa. Around town, everyone repeats the same rehearsed line: Lena drowned in 2003. Their identical phrasing chills him more than any lie would. Beat: creeping realization that grief here was scripted.

chapters.title: The Verdict Before the Crime
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In the courthouse basement he finds the original verdict — signed by then-clerk Aldous Vane, now chief judge — declaring a death that the coroner's log shows was never examined. Beat: the first hard proof that power rewrote memory.

chapters.title: Corliss Vanishes
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. His client misses their meeting; his flat has been searched, the advance payment left untouched but his copy of the inquest stolen. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve — someone believes the case is closable enough to kill for.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Tessa's POV. Tessa recalls the night of the supposed drowning: a woman running along the levee, a car idling, and Judge Vane's brother watching. She never told anyone because they made her feel mad. Beat: guilt and the courage to finally speak.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Trap
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He stages fake evidence in the shop and waits; a break-in confirms the conspirators are watching him — and leaves behind a warning note signed with the seal of the 2003 inquest. Beat: defiance kindling under threat.

chapters.title: A Witness Made of Paper
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Following paper trails, he learns 'Lena Marsh' appears in three different records with three different death dates — clerical fingerprints of deliberate erasure. Beat: grim delight; documents confess what people won't.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Judge
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Vane invites him to a courteous, menacing dinner, offering money and a subtle threat to the bookshop's lease. Juniper declines. Beat: the seduction of complicity refused, and the cost anticipated.

chapters.title: The Second Client
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A second client arrives — Vane's fixer, disguised, asking Juniper to confirm Lena is dead so the estate can be settled. Juniper plays along, buying time and learning the solstice 'murder' is really the final legal step to bury an appeal. Beat: dangerous double game.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Lena's POV (revealed). In a cabin upriver, a woman who has been dead for twenty years mails letters she never sends, watching the town through binoculars. She knows someone is asking about her. Beat: isolation cracking into hope.

chapters.title: The Statute Clock
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. His ally, young paralegal Dev, calculates that the appeal window closes at midnight on the solstice — the same hour as the staged 'murder.' Beat: urgency compressing every remaining thread.

chapters.title: Burned Archive
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The county archive burns overnight; Dev is hospitalized after being run off the road. Juniper realizes he kept one carbon copy hidden inside a rare book in his shop. Beat: loss, then the small fierce joy of outthinking them.

chapters.title: The Woman on the Levee
chapters.summary: Tessa's POV. Tessa sees the runner from her memory standing at the rail and follows her partway before losing her nerve — but leaves a note pinned where only a ghost would look. Beat: bridging fear and faith.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Alternating Juniper/Lena POVs. Using Tessa's note and the carbon copy, Juniper signals Lena through classified ads; she answers with a phrase only the real witness would know. Beat: two guarded strangers circling toward trust.

chapters.title: Twenty Years Underwater
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena tells her story: she witnessed Vane's brother kill a whistleblower, was declared dead to void her testimony, and has survived by staying buried. Beat: grief for a self she had to kill to stay alive.

chapters.title: The Price of Coming Back
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Resurfacing Lena means exposing her to the men who erased her; Corliss is found dead, having been her silent protector all along. Beat: mourning and the weight of the choice ahead.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The town prepares its anniversary memorial while Juniper, Lena, Tessa, and Dev assemble the case: carbon copy, coroner's log, Tessa's testimony. Vane's men sweep the streets. Beat: hushed tension before the storm.

chapters.title: The Hearing at Midnight
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the stroke of the statute's expiry, Juniper forces an emergency session by filing the appeal in open court, producing living witness Lena Marsh before the assembled town. Beat: triumphant reversal — the dead testifying.

chapters.title: Vane Unbound
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Cornered, Vane orders violence rather than face the record; his own clerk turns state's evidence, and his brother confesses to save himself. Vane is arrested on the courthouse steps. Beat: power curdling into ruin.

chapters.title: Reopening the Shop
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Weeks later, the bookshop reopens with a new sign: investigations accepted above the door. The town's memory begins honestly rewriting itself. Beat: quiet restoration and belonging earned.

chapters.title: Lena and the Verdict
chapters.summary: Shared Juniper/Lena POV. Lena formally reclaims her name at the registry; Juniper takes on a new client with an impossible case, and Lena takes the chair across the desk. Beat: forward motion — the verdict on their own lives finally theirs to write.
